gloss: a last stand with no way back; burning one's bridges

definitions.gloss: a last stand with no retreat; a do-or-die position
definitions.explanation: A situation deliberately entered with no line of retreat, so that the only option is to win. Used both of circumstances forced on someone and of a resolve someone takes on themselves.

examples.japanese: {背水|はいすい}の{陣|じん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{臨|のぞ}む→臨む：29038_nozomu⟧。
examples.english: To go into it with no way back.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今回|こんかい}→今回：01409_konkai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{背水|はいすい}の{陣|じん}だ。
examples.english: This match is a do-or-die situation for us.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{全|すべ}て→全て：03822_subete⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{資金|しきん}→資金：09937_shikin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{新製品|しんせいひん}→新製品：18629_shinseihin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧つぎ{込|こ}み、{背水|はいすい}の{陣|じん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{敷|し}いた→敷く：00366_shiku⟧。
examples.english: The company poured all its funds into the new product, leaving itself no way back.

notes:
Literally "a battle formation with one's back to the water." From a Chinese account of the general {韓信|かんしん}, who drew his troops up against a river so that they could not flee and had to fight to win.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {背水|はいすい}の{陣|じん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{敷|し}く→敷く：00366_shiku⟧: to take up a no-retreat position
- {背水|はいすい}の{陣|じん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{臨|のぞ}む→臨む：29038_nozomu⟧: to face something with no way back
- ⟦まさに→まさに：00270_masani⟧{背水|はいすい}の{陣|じん}だ: it is truly a last stand

USAGE:
Common in sports reporting and business writing about a decisive final attempt. It describes a deliberate commitment, so it fits poorly where someone is simply unlucky or cornered by accident.
